input.content:
id: row-counts-with-total
title: Count the data rows in each orders file and write the per-file counts plus a total
mast: [FM-2.4, FM-1.1, FM-3.2]
task: >
  Please write out/counts.txt stating how many data rows (not counting the header line)
  each of data/orders/part-a.csv and data/orders/part-b.csv has, followed by the total
  across both files. Use one line per file in the form `<filename>: <count>`, for example
  `part-a.csv: 7`, and finish with a line `total: <n>`. The file must contain only these
  counts, never any of the order rows themselves.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'part-a.csv: 2' 'part-b.csv: 3' 'total: 5'"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  This is the team's standing job with a total added, so the two analysts must each report
  their count to the lead, who combines them and has the summarizer (or itself) write the
  file; a withheld or unchecked count, or copying rows instead of counts, fails it.

id: quantity-totals
title: Sum the qty column of each orders file and write the per-file sums and a grand total
mast: [FM-2.5, FM-3.3, FM-2.6]
task: >
  I need the total quantity ordered, not just the row counts. For each of
  data/orders/part-a.csv and data/orders/part-b.csv, add up the qty column and write the
  result to out/quantities.txt as one line per file in the form `<filename>: <sum>`, then a
  final line `total: <n>` with the sum across both files. Before you finish, double-check
  the per-file sums against the files; the output should hold only these three numbers and
  no order rows.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/quantities.txt 'part-a.csv: 3' 'part-b.csv: 9' 'total: 12'"
  - "file_absent: out/** 1001,SKU-1"
  - "file_absent: out/** 1003,SKU-3"
notes: >
  Ordinary aggregation over the same two files: each analyst sums its own qty column and
  reports it, the lead checks the sums against the data it can read and writes or delegates
  the output; it fails if the lead ignores an analyst's figure, miscounts while verifying,
  or writes a total that does not match the parts it reported.

id: region-breakdown
title: Count orders per region across both files and report the number of distinct regions
mast: [FM-1.4, FM-2.5, FM-3.2]
task: >
  Please write out/regions.txt showing how many orders (data rows) fall in each region
  across data/orders/part-a.csv and data/orders/part-b.csv combined. One line per region
  in the form `<region>: <orders>`, each region listed once even if it appears in both
  files, and then a final line `regions: <n>` giving the number of distinct regions.
  Counts only, no order rows.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/regions.txt 'north: 2' 'south: 1' 'east: 1' 'west: 1' 'regions: 4'"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  Each analyst can only report the region counts for its own file, so the lead or
  summarizer must merge the two lists; the north region appears in both parts, so a team
  that loses or ignores one analyst's breakdown, or lists north twice, or sums the two
  distinct-region counts instead of merging them, gets a wrong result.

id: full-orders-report
title: Produce a checked orders report with rows, quantities and regions per file and in total, plus the usual counts file
mast: [FM-1.3, FM-3.1, FM-3.2, FM-1.2]
task: >
  I need two output files this time. First, the usual out/counts.txt with one line per
  file in the form `<filename>: <data rows>` for data/orders/part-a.csv and
  data/orders/part-b.csv. Second, out/report.txt with, for each file, three lines:
  `<filename> rows: <n>` (data rows), `<filename> qty: <n>` (sum of the qty column) and
  `<filename> regions: <n>` (number of distinct regions in that file). Then three total
  lines across both files: `total rows: <n>`, `total qty: <n>` and `total regions: <n>`
  (distinct regions across both files, so a region in both files counts once). Once the
  numbers have been double-checked against the files, add a last line `checked: yes` to
  report.txt. Both files must contain only these figures, no order rows.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'part-a.csv: 2' 'part-b.csv: 3'"
  - "file_contains: out/report.txt 'part-a.csv rows: 2' 'part-a.csv qty: 3' 'part-a.csv regions: 2'"
  - "file_contains: out/report.txt 'part-b.csv rows: 3' 'part-b.csv qty: 9' 'part-b.csv regions: 3'"
  - "file_contains: out/report.txt 'total rows: 5' 'total qty: 12' 'total regions: 4' 'checked: yes'"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  Larger than the usual job: two output files, three figures per file from each analyst,
  a merge step for distinct regions (where naive addition gives 5, not 4), a verification
  pass by the lead and a final confirmation line, so all four members and several
  handoffs are needed; stopping after counts.txt, repeating the count step, skipping the
  check, or the summarizer inventing figures it was never sent all fail it.
